name: declared_pins stops stripping quotes, so '3.12' never matches a bare 3.12
expect: a declared pin is read, quotes stripped

name: job_names runs past the jobs block, so a later top-level key reads as a job
edits:
if line and not line.startswith(" ") and not line.startswith("#"):
                break
expect: ...and a top-level key after jobs ends the block

name: job_blocks stops splitting, so a pin in ONE job is credited to its sibling
edits: end = ordered[idx + 1][1] if idx + 1 < len(ordered) else len(lines)
expect: a pin in a SIBLING job does not cover its neighbour

name: unpinned_jobs stops honouring the exemption list
expect: ...and an exempt job is not reported either

name: running_version drops the minor, so 3.12 and 3.14 look identical
expect: the running version is major.minor

name: the empty-corpus refusal goes, so a missing workflow dir reads as a pass
expect: no workflows at all is CANNOT RUN, never a pass

name: the no-pin-anywhere refusal goes — the precise state this guard exists to end
edits: return 2, ("CANNOT RUN — no `python-version:` was found in any workflow
return 0, ("CANNOT RUN — no `python-version:` was found in any workflow
expect: ...and so is a corpus with no pin anywhere

name: disagreeing pins stop failing, so guards and gates can run different interpreters
expect: ...and the message names both

name: an unpinned job stops failing, which is the whole subject of this guard
expect: ...and the failure names it

name: the in-CI VERSION check goes, so a pinned-but-wrong interpreter reports green
edits:
if running != pin:
            return 1, (f"FAILED — workflows pin {pin}, this interpreter is {running}.")

if False:
            return 1, (f"FAILED — workflows pin {pin}, this interpreter is {running}.")
expect: ...and it still FAILS when provenance is fine but the VERSION is wrong

name: the local advisory becomes a FAILURE, which is how a gate gets switched off
expect: ...but LOCALLY the same mismatch is ADVISORY and exits 0

name: the step's ACTION is no longer checked, so any step's with: block counts as a pin
expect: ...nor is one in an UNRELATED action's with: block

name: pin_took_effect answers True with no evidence, so an unexported location reads as pinned
expect: pin_took_effect says None when nothing exported a location

name: the provenance test loses its separator, so a sibling directory counts as under it
expect: ...and a sibling directory sharing a PREFIX is not under it

name: the no-provenance refusal goes, so a version match alone passes for the pin taking effect
expect: IN CI, a matching VERSION with no provenance FAILS — the ambient python matches too

name: the wrong-interpreter refusal goes, which is update-environment: false reporting green
expect: ...and an interpreter NOT under the exported location FAILS, which is update-environment: false

name: asserts_here arms everywhere, turning the local advisory into a failure
expect: ...and its absence does not

name: the unreadable-job refusal goes, so an invisible job among readable ones passes
expect: ...and a workflow containing one is CANNOT RUN even though another job IS readable

name: the pin need not be under with:, so an env: entry counts as an action input
expect: a python-version under env: in the setup-python step is NOT a pin

name: the unreadable-job COUNT is dropped, so only an all-or-nothing file refuses
expect: ...and a workflow containing one is CANNOT RUN even though another job IS readable

name: the inline-comment strip goes, so a commented pin reds the required check with nonsense
expect: an inline comment on the pin line is stripped from the VALUE

name: an EMPTY exported location is treated as provenance — fail-open for every absolute path
expect: an EMPTY exported location is no evidence, not proof of provenance

name: the trailing slash is no longer trimmed, so a slashed location breaks provenance
expect: ...and a trailing slash on the location does not break it

name: the equality arm goes, so the location itself stops counting as under itself
expect: ...and the location itself, as an executable, counts as under it

name: the .yaml half of the corpus is dropped, so such a workflow is never read at all
expect: the corpus reads both workflow extensions
